title: polyglot credential orchestrator and stream consumer clarity
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: customers reported subtle race conditions during token refresh when long-running streaming consumers reattached to new credentials; SDK teams saw duplicated refresh logic and divergent ergonomics across Python/TS/Go. Motivation: unify credential refresh orchestration, reduce repeated token-fetch boilerplate, and smooth streaming consumer ergonomics (backpressure and resume) with a minimal compatibility surface. Summary: introduce a CredOrchestrator abstraction (polyglot spec + lightweight runtime helper implementations in each SDK), a StreamSeat helper that centralizes pause/resume/backpressure hints for async iterators/streams, and small API parity tweaks to reduce cognitive load between SDKs. The change keeps the public TokenProvider interface backward-compatible but deprecates the legacy TokenCallback for easier migration. Implementation details: 1) CredOrchestrator - single-responsibility component that sequences credential refresh, exposes lease windows and a Subscribe/Lease semantics for consumers to receive pre-emptive refresh events; built to be sync-friendly in Go, awaitable in TS, and async/await in Python. 2) StreamSeat - ergonomic wrapper over existing streaming iterators that provides an opt-in 'seat' handle for consumers to signal sustained backpressure and to request graceful drain and reconnects (used by caller-side retry policies). 3) Compact adapters - small compatibility shims in each SDK to map existing TokenProvider implementations to the CredOrchestrator model; included helper for rolling-window refresh to avoid thundering herd on refresh. 4) Migration & docs - add a migration guide with patterns for long-lived streams and sample recipes. 5) Version bumps - python->1.12.0, typescript->1.8.0, go->1.5.3. Test & validation: unit tests for lease behavior and integration tests that simulate token expiry mid-stream across all three SDKs; canary run against internal realtime testbed for 48h. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-4921) linked - [x] SDK implementations (py/ts/go) compiled and smoke-tested - [x] E2E canary run (48h) - [x] Migration docs and examples - [x] Version bumps and changelogs Notes: kept surface minimal, no breaking contract changes for existing TokenProvider consumers; introduced deprecation warnings where appropriate.
